goz: Wellness Services Regulation · 4 July 2026 · Official Gazette 33300
ozet: Article 17 of the regulation leaves the international health tourism authorisation of esenlik centres and units to the Ministry's determination. This tool measures the effect of that determination not having been made.
s1_n: The structure of the network comes from the planning criteria of Article 10(1). The probability tables are not written by hand; they are learned from the records below. Adding a record retrains the model.
veri_ornek: The starter set is not real intake data; it was constructed from domain rules and is expected to be replaced with real records.
veri_yok: No records. The model cannot be trained.
model_n: Select a node. The columns show the learned probabilities and the last figure how many observations the row rests on.
model_zayif: rows resting on fewer than five observations
ornek_b: Draw a profile from the model
ornek_n: The network is traversed in topological order; at each node a draw is made from the row matching the parent values.
s2_n: Applications first pass the structural rules; those failing area, room, permit or responsible-manager conditions receive no licence. Licensed centres are then assessed against the Annex 4 inspection rules.
m_yapisal: Share of applications meeting the licence conditions
m_denetim: Share of centres complying with the inspection rules
s3_b: Generating synthetic visitors and applying them to the centres
s3_n: Visitors are drawn from the trained model, then matched against the centres one by one. The outcome is three-valued. Going unserved arises from two kinds of cause: the convalescence bar (Article 10(8)(d)) is a regulatory prohibition, while finding no centre offering the service sought and finding those centres at capacity are matters of supply not meeting demand. An undefined outcome arises from three distinct gaps: for residents abroad, no determination has been made under Article 17; convalescence is left undefined in Article 10(8)(d); and Article 4(1)(c) gives no criterion for treatment purpose. Only the first is resolved by the scenarios.
z_istah: Share of centres accepting visitors from abroad while undefined
s4_n: This tab draws on three separate sources. The matching strip, the provisions table and the segment breakdown come from the run you just made. The sensitivity analysis is computed separately on its own fixed baseline. The multi-year projection was computed in advance and is unaffected by any setting in your session. An undefined outcome is a match where no rule is violated but the status remains undetermined because of a gap in the regulation; the breakdown by source is given separately below.
proj_b: Multi-year projection — a separate, precomputed run
proj_n: This section does not concern the centres and visitors you generated above. The ten-year course of the five scenarios was computed separately and embedded in the page; the simulation regenerates its own centres and visitors every year. These charts are unaffected by any setting in your session. The solid line is the median, the shaded area the 10–90 percentile range across repetitions.
g_uyum: Centres in good or fair compliance
g_yurtdisi: Share of visitors from abroad served
u1: There is no data to project a sector one month old across ten years. Entry rate, demand growth and compliance behaviour are assumptions. What matters is the difference between scenarios, not the absolute numbers.
u2: All centres and visitors are synthetic. No real person or institution data is used.
u3: Twenty-one inspection rules come from Annex 4 of the Wellness Services Regulation and twelve structural rules from the articles. The binding text is the Official Gazette.
mal_n: The cost of the conditions imposed by the regulation varies by centre type. The figures are not real market data but relative units, scalable with the slider below. A centre whose revenue does not cover its cost cannot survive in the long run.
mal_secili: Cost breakdown of the selected centre
duy_n: Each parameter is moved to its lower and upper value in turn and the change in the outcome is measured. A long bar means that outcome depends heavily on that parameter. Making the influence of free parameters visible is more honest than hiding it.
bel_n: A catalogue produced by reading the text article by article. Each entry marks a gap that prevents a provision from being applied on its own. Four of these fourteen entries are wired into the simulation: the determination under Article 17, the undefined notion of convalescence and the missing criterion for treatment purpose produce an undefined outcome at the matching stage, while the missing criterion for appropriate premises does so at the licensing stage. Only the uncertainty under Article 17 is resolved by the scenarios; the other three persist in every scenario. The remaining ten are identified but not modelled.
r_neden_hizmet_yok: No centre offers the service sought
r_neden_kapasite_dolu: Centres offering it are at capacity
r_neden_10/8-d: Wellness services may not be provided in convalescence (Article 10(8)(d))
r_neden_17/1: No determination made on the international health tourism authorisation (Article 17)
d1: Article 17 provides that the procedures for the international health tourism authorisation of esenlik centres and units are to be determined by the Ministry. The Regulation on International Health Tourism (26/4/2025) requires an authorisation certificate, but whether the esenlik centre licence meets that regulation's definition of a health facility has not been determined. In addition, none of the twenty-one questions in Annex 4 of the Wellness Services Regulation concerns this matter. A match involving a visitor resident abroad therefore cannot be classified as compliant or non-compliant.
m_ihlal_not: For most rules Annex 4 prescribes a warning and an administrative fine at the first detection, and the centre continues to operate. Only rules whose first detection suspends operations remove a centre from matching.
m_askida_not: Article 10(4) requires premises appropriate to the nature of the service but gives no criterion for appropriateness. In these applications the licence can neither be granted nor refused; the decision is left pending. No scenario resolves this.
r_neden_10/8-d-gri: Undetermined because convalescence is not defined (Article 10(8)(d))
r_neden_4/1-c-tedavi: Undetermined whether the service counts as treatment under a heavy chronic burden (Article 4(1)(c))
bel_kaynak_n: Which gap each undefined match arises from. Only the uncertainty under Article 17 is resolved by the scenarios; the other two persist in every scenario.
bel_mod_not: Four of the fourteen catalogue entries are wired into the simulation. Three produce an undefined outcome at the matching stage and one at the licensing stage. The remaining ten are identified but not modelled.
